📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," stated local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

The ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

It has been revealed that "In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," noted council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site.".

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property.".

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

California's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

Today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

Under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," said Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

Miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

Industry observers note that LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman said energy companies were prepared to challenge the new ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," mentioned Zierman.

The relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

Even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

California's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

When wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

The cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging plans or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

It has been revealed that but those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is notes both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air.".

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Virgil van Dijk admitted he is unsure whether he will extend his Liverpool contract beyond the end of this season.

The Reds captain's current deal expires in June 2027, with an Anfield exit potentially on the cards for the 35-year-old.

Van Dijk joined Liverpool from Southampton in January 2018 and has gone on to make 389 appearances for the club.

The Netherlands international has won two Premier League titles, one Champions League, one Super Cup, one Club World Cup, two EFL Cups and one FA Cup during his time on Merseyside.

Liverpool continue the 2026-27 season with a clash against rivals Manchester United on Sunday.

Should he start this match, Van Dijk will be starting a 50th consecutive Premier League game for Liverpool, the fourth time he has had a run of 50+ unbroken starts in the competition – the joint-most by an outfield player along with Sylvain Distin.

Aged 35 years and 137 days, he would also become the oldest outfield player to start 50+ consecutive Premier League games for a single club, overtaking Kevin Davies for Bolton (67 in a row aged 34y 175d).

While Van Dijk feels he is capable of playing for "many more years", it is yet to be decided how long he will remain at Liverpool.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk told Sky Sports.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:27.

Tottenham Hotspur have shared footage of Lucas Bergvall and Savio back in training ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The pair have both missed each of Spurs' last four Premier League matches, having picked up injuries ahead of October's 3-1 home victory over Coventry City.

Savio has been dealing with a muscular problem, while Bergvall has been nursing a knee injury, but Roberto De Zerbi expressed hope that the pair would return following the November international break.

On Friday, Spurs posted a 55-second clip on social media showing Savio and Bergvall in training with their teammates, taking part in warm-up exercises and drills with the ball at their feet.

Sávio and Bergvall in training ? ? @Betano_UK https://t.co/3Iug9LlBjf.

De Zerbi then confirmed at his pre-game press conference that the Brazilian attacker and Swedish midfielder are fine to feature against Ipswich, as well as assuring that James Maddison is fit and ready.

However, none of Mykhaylo Mudryk, Tosin Adarabioyo or Mathys Tel will be ready just yet, as the latter is still feeling the effects of the crunching tackle from Jayden Bogle in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United two weekends ago.

In a recent development, "Bergvall, Maddison and Savio are back," De Zerbi stated. "Tosin and Mathys Tel no. Tosin is already okay but it is not the right moment to take any risks and Mathys Tel, we need another two or three weeks. Mudryk is not ready yet.".

With Tel sidelined for another two or three weeks, the Frenchman could miss each of Tottenham's next four matches, including the North London derby against Arsenal on December 6.

The Lilywhites will also have to cope without the attacker against Sunderland and Fulham on November 29 and December 3 respectively, and it also remains to be seen if Mudryk will be fit for those clashes after the Chelsea loanee burned bridges with a few Tottenham fans.

In a recent interview, Mudryk reflected on his yearning to join Tottenham's bitter rivals Arsenal in 2024, before Chelsea won the race to sign him from Shakhtar Donetsk.

"Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” Mudryk Ukrainian podcast Guest of Gordon. "Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream.

“There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal. The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money. But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on.".

In a recent development, while De Zerbi admitted he could understand Tottenham fans' frustrations, he leapt to the defence of his long-term colleague, adding: "Yes I can understand but Mudryk is a good guy, a good player, he suffered a lot with the situation in the last couple of years. He has to do one thing, show on the pitch his qualities.".

Tottenham head into the weekend in 11th place in the Premier League table, just three points shy of Bournemouth in seventh spot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England captain Harry Kane is facing three months out with an ankle injury, Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has confirmed.

The Ballon d’Or winner scored against both Croatia and Spain in the international break and was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders in all competitions at the Allianz Arena.

However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise’s deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane had a quick exchange with Kompany, back in the Bayern hot-seat for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.

Speaking at full-time, Kompany confirmed Kane was facing months on the sidelines with what Max Eberl described as a tear of the syndesmotic ligament.

Sky Germany has reported he can expect to spend three months on the sidelines, meaning he will hope return before England face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

Matters only grew worse for Bayern thereafter, as Olise was also forced off shortly after Kane with an ankle injury of his own. He was able to walk off the pitch before treatment, though.

Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore opened the scoring for Cologne after just 12 minutes, but the match finished 1-1 as Nathaniel Brown equalised for the hosts before the break.

Bayern Munich have opened the door to selling Jamal Musiala, or renegotiating his contract, amid concerns he may struggle to get back to his best form after being diagnosed with a fainting condition.

Musiala, 23, left the footballing world deeply concerned in August when he collapsed on-pitch twice in the span of just a few days, during pre-season friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig.

It has been revealed that he later revealed in a statement that he had been diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction”, adding: “(These episodes) are currently simply part of my everyday life. I am receiving the best possible medical care in this regard, and I am very optimistic... there is no additional health risk beyond this.”.

Musiala has since appeared in four league matches, three cup ties, and one Champions League match, tallying two goals and two assists in those appearances.

Bayern Munich’s decision-makers, though, are beginning to worry that Musiala, one of Bayern’s best-paid players, may not be able to replicate the form of his youth.

The club has opened the door to selling the former Chelsea youngster Musiala in upcoming transfer windows, though they acknowledge it may be hard to find a buyer given the player’s condition.

It has been revealed that speaking on Friday evening, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told Sky Germany: “(Musiala) has a health-related matter. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal.

“What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.”.

Musiala earns a reported wage of €25m (£20.9m) per year. Until Harry Kane signed a lucrative new contract in November, he was Bayern’s best-paid player, which Rummenigge fears may prove unsustainable.

Rummenigge continued: “[We need to] talk to the player, to the family and, above all, to the agency, because, with all due respect, those sums are then no longer feasible.”.

“I think we’ve handled the player’s situation very carefully, and we all want him to return, ideally in the best possible shape.

#14519. Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia

Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.
  • The Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again.
  • "Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," said Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, announced shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.

The Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again. They had been barred from doing so since shortly after Russia debuted its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," said Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.

"Several championships are only weeks away, and changes to participation affect many people; players, teams, organizing committees and host cities," he remarked. "We will work closely with all of them to find practical solutions.".

Recent findings suggest that the first tournament the CAS decision applies to is the World Juniors, to be held beginning on December 26 in Canada. Just how it will affect the tournament is not clear. Hockey Canada remarked it was in contact with the IIHF and had briefed Prime Minister Mark Carney's government on the decision.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand told public broadcaster CBC that she is "not comfortable" with allowing a Russian team to take part in the tournament in Alberta.

"This is a very unwelcome decision given the geopolitical situation, given the actions of Russia," she said. "All options are on the table, and I will say, again, I greet this decision with great disappointment.".

Canada's secretary of state for sport, Adam van Koeverden, appeared to rule out Russian athletes being granted visas for the tournament.

"Canada will maintain restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes at events hosted in Canada that receive funding from the Government of Canada and explore further options to ensure that the Russian government is held accountable," he said in a statement.

Germany is also considering its options as it prepares to host the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Düsseldorf and Mannheim in May.

"The German government takes a very critical view of the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, a government spokesman remarked on Sunday, according to the DPA news agency.

"The German government will discuss possible consequences of the ruling, including for the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany, with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) promptly.".

In a recent development, the DEB's chief executive, Frank Lutz, is to travel to Berlin to discuss the matter with government officials this week. Speaking on broadcaster MagentaSport on the weekend, he conceded that surrendering Germany's hosting rights for the lucrative tournament was a possibility.

"I do not want to paint a black picture. I do not want to call the World Championship into question either. But of course, we at the DEB also have to consider the option of handing back this championship," he said.

Several other national ice hockey federations have expressed disappointment at the CAS decision, including those of Ukraine, Sweden, Finland, and Czechia.

The International Olympic Committee opened the door for Russian athletes to return to international competition when it lifted its ban of the Russian Olympic Committee in July. However, the IIHF had already decided to continue to exclude Russian teams for the 2026-27 season – over security concerns. The CAS decision – handed down after an appeal by Russia – found this reasoning was insufficiently proven.

The Kremlin's reaction to the ruling was, unsurprisingly, positive.

"Russia is returning to world hockey. This place rightfully belongs to us, and discrimination in hockey has been brought to an end," Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told state television channel Vesti.

A boycott of the World Juniors, Men's World Championships or other tournaments by individual nations is now emerging as a real possibility.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen remarked in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday evening.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

By Tuesday afternoon, the Finland-led effort was gaining steam, with Sweden, Norway and Denmark making similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said in a statement.

This came shortly after Norway noted it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

In a recent development, "Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors tournament.

There has been the suggestion, that having won this victory at the CAS, Russia's next focus could be on football, where its national and club teams remain excluded from international competitions.

Russian FA general secretary Maxim Mitrofanov told state news agency Tass that there "should be one rule for all.".

World football's governing body FIFA allowed a Russia boys' team to play under its national flag in the inaugural Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, which kicked off last week and ends on Saturday.

In a recent development, this article was originally published on November 2, 2026. It was updated on November 3 with the statement from the Finnish Ice Hockey Association. It was later updated with the statements from the Swedish, Norwegian and Danish federations.

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6420 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • In a recent development, mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

In a recent development, mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Industry observers note that that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

Industry observers note that on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

Sources indicate that it could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

Sources indicate that the irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

According to recent reports, the manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

Industry observers note that england attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as significant as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Recent findings suggest that maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

MAJOR SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Industry observers note that then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

It could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was promptly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not strategy to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

Industry observers note that “We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

Recent findings suggest that “We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

In a recent development, “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

According to recent reports, A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that “This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

Sources indicate that “There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

England’s prepares for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel said. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

Recent findings suggest that “For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

Declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

It has been revealed that trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against Fresh Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

In a recent development, having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

According to recent reports, ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but rapidly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Recent findings suggest that salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

They are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ says Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Sources indicate that grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

According to recent reports, ‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady mentioned that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

In a recent development, intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

Recent findings suggest that city have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

He utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

Recent findings suggest that the format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

#14514. Tech Report: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

Tech Report: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.
  • In a recent development, four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools.
  • Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.

In a recent development, four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools. They have sold a further €37 billion ($41 billion) of bonds in euros.

Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.

Sources indicate that next year, Goldman Sachs projects that total fresh AI hyperscaler bond sales are expected to reach $420 billion. About €60 billion will be issued in euros, according to Dutch bank ING.

That is unwelcome news for European companies and countries like France, Germany and Italy, whose sovereign bond yields have risen sharply in recent months and are already straining public finances.

It has been revealed that with public debt at 119% of gross domestic product (GDP) and a deficit still running above 5%, France is already paying a sizable risk premium on its debt. Over the past six months, yields on French 10-year bonds have climbed from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5%.

The French government's interest bill is set to rise from €79 billion at the moment to €91 billion next year and over €100 billion by 2028.

Based on these figures alone, France's Finance Ministry needs to find tens of billions of euros in additional cuts, tax hikes, or more borrowing by the end of the decade.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank said the euro bond market was adapting well to the presence of AI giants but warned they "could make it harder for other companies and other economic sectors to access finance.".

Writing in a blog post, they also questioned whether the bloc's financial markets can "smoothly handle such large and concentrated debt inflows and warned of a "potential spillover to the sovereign and supranational segment of the bond market.".

That means governments and international lenders such as the European Union and the European Investment Bank could also end up paying more to borrow.

Viktor Hjort, global head of credit strategy at the French bank BNP Paribas, described the phenomenon as "bond abundance.".

Hjort told DW that the presence of the hyperscalers in the euro bond market is "already high enough to create competition" within the corporate sector and "between corporates and governments for available fixed income funds." These are investment funds that mostly buy bonds, which pay regular interest.

Bond yields jumped again last month, driven by rebounding energy prices linked to the Iran war and France’s political crisis, which Hjort stated further revealed the growing competition for capital, as government and organization borrowing costs rose together.

Normally, nervous investors move into government bonds during uncertain times, which pushes their borrowing costs down.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Goldman Sachs warned last week that rising interest costs were starting to hurt earnings at European companies. Among firms in the Stoxx 600 — an index of 600 large, mid-sized and small companies across Europe — Goldman found that interest costs as a share of sales have risen by nearly half since 2022.

The bank's analysts said this had cut earnings by more than 5% over the same period.

Factor in the competition from AI bonds, and European firms could now face pressure to cut their investments in new plants, equipment and research, as well as shareholder payouts, to prioritize loan repayments.

Industry observers note that the pressure doesn't stop at national governments. Europe's cities and regions, whose borrowing helps to fund schools, transport and infrastructure, may also feel the effects of the AI boom.

A study for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development(OECD), published in January, compared local bond markets in Belgium, Germany, Spain, Sweden and Canada. Where AI was spreading fastest, measured by the share of AI-related job vacancies, borrowing costs for cities and regions tended to rise.

"Whereas in the United States, my research has found that AI investments are linked to a lower cost of borrowing for municipalities, the opposite appears to hold in several European countries," the study's co-author, Christos Makridis of Arizona State University's W. P. Carey School of Business, told DW.

While AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's widening fiscal strains, US Big Tech's huge appetite for capital could add further pressure next year, due to the additional billions in latest bonds planned.

The irony is that European taxpayers could end up paying more on their own governments' debt, partly to help finance an AI boom across the Atlantic.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, stated the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

It has been revealed that santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Sources indicate that given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 14:35, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:09.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly interested in signing Inter Milan midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu.

After enjoying a memorable spell at AC Milan, Calhanoglu switched to their cross-city rivals Inter in the summer of 2021 and has since made 225 appearances across all competitions.

The highly-skilled central midfielder has scored 53 goals and registered 39 assists for Inter, while continuing to impress with his performances this season.

However, his contract situation has cast doubt over his long-term future at the club, with several sides, including Tottenham, reportedly looking to take advantage of the uncertainty.

The Turkish international has a contract at San Siro until 2027, but he is yet to receive an offer to extend his stay.

The 32-year-old wants to continue with Inter, although doing so could require him to accept a significant pay cut, something he is currently unwilling to consider.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, Tottenham are ready to welcome the midfielder, but face competition from Galatasaray, Juventus and Como.

Spurs spent heavily during the summer transfer window to overhaul their midfield, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on big-money deals.

After a nightmare start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi's side are gradually climbing the table and presently sit 11th in the Premier League table with 12 points from 10 matches.

De Zerbi already has plenty of midfield options at his disposal, but it appears he wants a technically gifted and versatile player with proven experience, making Calhanoglu an attractive option.

Calhanoglu operates primarily as a defensive midfielder, although his creative qualities remain a significant asset.

Furthermore, the former Bayer Leverkusen midfielder is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting and could adapt well to the Premier League, even at this stage of his career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola was sort of thrown in the deep end when he took over from Arne Slot as Liverpool's manager.

The Reds were coming off the back of a fifth-place finish in the Premier League, a result which ended with Slot being relieved of his duties.

Fenway Sports Group knew that they had to get their next appointment right which is why fans were so happy with the Spaniard being appointed.

His heavy metal style of football and his previous Premier League experience looked like two of the main reasons why he was perfectly suited to the role.

However, since his appointment, things have been a bit topsy-turvy with Liverpool even losing to Fenerbahce in the Premier League.

This caused many questions to arise with the upcoming transfer windows now seeming rather important.

Atletico Madrid will not sign Martin Zubimendi which could stop Pablo Barrios from joining Liverpool.

On the Ukrainian national team and their federation, the Ukrainian Association of Football, Mudryk said: ‘I’ll be honest, it pretended to help. But in reality, there was no help. They created more problems than they solved. Especially when we needed help the most, they turned their backs on us.

Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken publicly for the first time about the doping case that cost him two years of his career.

Mudryk has criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football over their support during his case.

Daily Mail Sport contacted the Ukrainian Association of Football for comment.

Distancing themselves from their own player, not helping, pretending to help, and in the end, first they drag the case out for months without really helping the case in the end. But at least the UAF isn’t to blame.’.

It has been revealed that mudryk was handed an initial four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance prior to that coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. Mudryk appeared for Chelsea during their pre-season tour before joining Tottenham on loan.

On how and why he failed his test, Mudryk said: ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It’s a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe.

‘This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that’s Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

‘I was at home and Chelsea’s management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you’ve returned a positive doping test and now you’re facing a ban.

According to recent reports, ‘You can’t believe it’s true. You can’t believe this is happening to you. If I’d ever taken anything anywhere, I’d have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

Sources indicate that ‘At least I’d have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that’s the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

‘Otherwise there’d be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don’t hear them.

Mudryk returned to action when his ban was lifted in August, with the winger revealing Xabi Alonso told him to get game time and that he was 'counting on him'.

The Ukrainian joined Tottenham on loan but has seen injury restrict his involvement to date.

Recent findings suggest that ‘At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you’re falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You’re flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don’t wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.’.

Recent findings suggest that mudryk revealed how ‘the figure is in the millions’ when asked about the lawyers fees which were needed to fight his case. He confirmed he paid for that himself, along with the personal trainers and massage therapists he used to maintain his fitness while suspended. However, Mudryk did add that Chelsea continued to pay his salary during his time out of football.

On joining Tottenham and being reunited with Roberto De Zerbi, who formerly managed him at Shakhtar Donetsk, Mudryk said: ‘It’s a perfectly logical decision. The club (Chelsea) has a new coach (Xabi Alonso), he sees football his own way. He sees the players he needs for that football. He came up and told me straight to my face: “You’d better go and play, get some game time, and then come back to Chelsea. I’m counting on you.”’ On De Zerbi, he added: ‘We met and he says: “Are you happy? Come on, we’ve still got a lot of work to do together.”’.

It has been revealed that mudryk added how difficult it was after switching to England and, along with encountering challenges with his former representatives who encouraged him to move to Chelsea rather than Arsenal, he remarked: 'They give you ultimatums, you know. That’s how it is.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The AFC cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions" caused by conflicts in the region.
  • Sources indicate that instead of January 7, 2027, the tournament will now kick off on December 23 and end on January 21, 2028.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A little over two months before it was set to kick off, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed its flagship international football tournament in the wake of recent deadly attacks on host country, Saudi Arabia.

The AFC cited "substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions" caused by conflicts in the region.

Sources indicate that instead of January 7, 2027, the tournament will now kick off on December 23 and end on January 21, 2028. The postponement follows delays and cancellations of a number of sporting events in the region, including a Formula One race, the men's and women's tennis finals, the 2027 Dakar Rally and disruption to Asia's marquee continental club football tournament, the AFC Champions League Elite.

Saudi Arabia hosted, and won, the Gulf Cup last month, but there had already been much talk about whether the much larger Asian Cup could go ahead.

In a recent development, it was scheduled to feature 24 teams playing matches in eight venues across Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar. However, the AFC said that "circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions," made the tournament impossible.

"Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organization and delivery of the competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.".

According to recent reports, in particular, the postponement was forced by a recent wave of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi rebels as well as other raging conflicts in the region. The Houthis have targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports. They are fighting a Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognized government, a civil war that reignited in July following a years-long truce.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AFC had been under pressure from several federations to postpone the tournament, with South Korea's players leading the way.

"The ongoing military tensions and security instability in the Middle East are issues that cannot be taken lightly," Lee Keun-ho, president of the Korea Professional Footballers Association, noted last month, according to the Yonhap News Agency.

Lee added that "no tournament's value can take precedence over the lives and safety of players and football fans.".

In a recent development, it seems that the AFC now agrees. However, following the announcement of the postponement, Yasser al-Misehal, chairman of the local organizing committee, promised that Saudi Arabia was "fully ready" whenever the tournament ended up being held.

"The tournament will move to the fresh dates, and our preparations will continue as planned," he told the Saudi Press Agency.

"We're working closely with the AFC and all our partners to make sure the tournament runs smoothly and meets the high standards expected of Saudi Arabia and the Asian Cup.".

Saudi Arabia has invested hugely in sports over the last decade, from owning Premier League teams to hosting boxing title fights and bidding for a number of major sporting events, most notably World Cup 2034, which they won the right to host unopposed.

However, the country has recently withdrawn or slashed funding for a number of sporting events including golf, rugby, tennis and winter sports.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Recent findings suggest that russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

In a recent development, toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

Sources indicate that “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Sources indicate that verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a latest floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car revision since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
